The Reform Congregation Keneseth Israel (KI), also known as Keneseth Israel Temple or KI Temple, is a Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue located in Elkins Park, Pennsylvania. It was founded in Philadelphia in 1847 and is recognized as the sixth-oldest Reform congregation in the country.

The congregation has a rich history dating back to 1900 when it became one of the largest Reform congregations in the United States by that time. The synagogue occupied several locations in Philadelphia before constructing a building on North Broad Street in 1891, and later relocated to its current site in Elkins Park in 1956.

The congregation has been led by eight rabbis since its founding: David Einhorn, Joseph Krauskopf, Bertram Korn, Simeon Maslin (who served as the president of the Central Conference of American Rabbis from 1995 to 1997), and Lance J. Sussman who is currently the senior rabbi.

Notable members of the congregation include Benjamin Netanyahu, Arlin Adams, Edward R. Becker, Jan E. DuBois, Horace Stern, members of the Gimbel family, Lessing J. Rosenwald, William S. Paley, Simon Guggenheim, and Walter Annenberg. Albert Einstein accepted honorary membership in 1934.

The history of KI Temple traces back to 1847 when Julius Stern led its establishment as a Reform congregation. It has been actively serving Philadelphia’s Jewish community for over 200 years since then.
